To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the bone‐marrows of patients with malignant melanoma, especially those with clinical Stage II, should be biopsied routinely as part of their preoperative evaluation, and that this procedure can be done with a Jansen needle.

1) the chest X ray was of value in preoperative screening; 2) the value of the liver, brain, bone, and bone marrow scans was questionable; and 3) the bone‐mar row biopsy done with a Jansen‐Hepner needle was of value.
the bone‐mar-row biopsy is the only useful test in preoperative screening in patients with malignant melanoma.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in the preopertive screening of patients with clinical Stage I or Stage I human malignant melanoma there is no need for a bone‐marrow aspirate, brain scan, liver scan, or bone scan.
the preoperative screening procedures for malignant melanoma are not as valuable as they are for other malignancies.
the preoperative bone‐marrow aspirate and biopsy is of value in detecting occult metastases in the bone marrow in patients with clinical Stage II malignant melanoma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the bone‐marrows of 50 patients with Stage I and II melanoma were examined.

the value of preoperative scanning procedures for patients with malignant melanoma is questionable, and that a bone‐marrow aspirate should be done in all patients with Stage II disease and considered in those with Stage I disease.

in patients with clinical Stage I melanoma, the preoperative bone‐marrow examination was negative in 30 of 30 patients, while in those with clinical Stage II, the bone marrow was positive in one of 20 patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the preoperative screening procedures should be done on all patients with Stage II malignant melanoma and that in the case of patients with Stage II disease, bone‐marrow biopsies should be done in addition to other screening procedures.
bone‐marrow biopsies are an essential part of the preoperative workup in patients with Stage II disease.
a Janshindi needle biopsy of the bone marrow should be done in all patients with clinical Stage II melanoma prior to surgery to rule out the possibility of metastatic disease.
